ru: Я была́ в гостя́х у ба́бушки.
note: Reported in #609. The primary keeps "at Grandma's"; dropping the "at" is the same sentence in the plainer register, and word-bank answers are graded as a bag of words, so the shorter rendering was failing outright rather than being read as a variant.

ru: Де́ти бы́стро оде́лись и пошли́ в шко́лу.
en_alt: The children dressed quickly and went to school.
note: Reported in #595. Intransitive "dressed" is the ordinary English for «оде́лись» and carries the same reflexive sense as "got dressed"; only the extra "got" separated the learner's answer from the primary, and bag-of-words grading counts that as a missing word.

en_alt: Many cars are in the street.
note: Reported in #594. English existentials need a dummy "there" that «мно́го» has no counterpart for, so learners assemble the sentence without it. This rendering carries the same words as that answer, which lets the drill's right-words-different-order path ask the learner to confirm instead of marking it wrong.

en_alt: Many trainers are in the shop.
note: Reported in #593, the same dummy-"there" shape as «На у́лице мно́го автомоби́лей.» above: the Russian has nothing the "there" translates, so the assembled answer omits it.

en_alt: The city is still a long way off.
note: Reported in #729. «До го́рода ещё далеко́» says the distance is still great; turning the city into the subject is the commoner English, and the word bank failed it outright because the primary's dummy "it" and "to" have no place in it.

en_alt: Many different juices are in the shop.
note: Reported in #720. As #594: English needs a dummy "there" that «мно́го» has no counterpart for, so learners build the sentence without it. This rendering carries the same words as that answer, so the drill's right-words-different-order path asks the learner to confirm instead of marking it wrong.

en_alt: Many vegetables are in the soup.
note: Reported in #739. The same existential "there" as #594 and #720; this rendering lets an answer without it reach the confirm step.

en_alt: Good news was in the letter.
note: Reported in #839. The same existential "there" as #594; this rendering lets an answer without it reach the confirm step.

en: The film begins at eight. (that's the timetable)
note: Reported in #723. In the aspect contrast drill "The film begins at eight" read as well for «начнётся» — this showing, once — as for the timetable imperfective the sentence uses. The bracketed note is a label the graders ignore (#783), so it disambiguates the prompt without becoming a word anyone must type.
